        df_list.append(pmid_df)

# 2. PubTator3 Search (Entity highlighting, fallback)
pubtator_results = []
for page in range(1, 1 + 1):
    search_results = pubtator_api_search_papers(
        boolean_query_text='"Exome sequencing identifies novel apolipoprotein B" hypobetalipoproteinemia type 1 diabetes',
        relation_query=None,
        page=page,
        max_retries=3,
        max_requests_per_second=3
    )
    if search_results is not None and not search_results.empty:
        pubtator_results.append(search_results)
    else:
        break

if pubtator_results:
    pubtator_df = pd.concat(pubtator_results)
    if "Highlighted_Text" in pubtator_df.columns:
        pubtator_df = pubtator_df.rename(columns={"Highlighted_Text": "Abstract"})
    
    for col in ["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]:
        if col not in pubtator_df.columns:
            pubtator_df[col] = ""
    pubtator_df = pubtator_df[["PMID", "Title", "Journal", "Year", "Abstract"]]
    df_list.append(pubtator_df)

# 3. Combine, Deduplicate and Format Clean Output
if df_list:
    final_df = pd.concat(df_list).reset_index(drop=True)
    # Deduplicate by PMID, keeping the first occurrence (which guarantees PubMed relevance is maintained)
    final_df = final_df.drop_duplicates(subset=["PMID"], keep="first")
    
    # Optional: Save to CSV for persistent logging
    final_df.to_csv('/home/data4/xiangyu/BioDSA/workdir/workdir/exact_article.csv', index=False)
    print(f"The search results are saved at '/home/data4/xiangyu/BioDSA/workdir/workdir/exact_article.csv'")
    print(f"Total results found: {len(final_df)}\n")
    print("=" * 80)
    print("TOP RESULTS (Showing up to 15 most relevant):")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    # FORMAT FOR LLM: Clean text layout rather than Markdown table
    for idx, row in final_df.head(15).iterrows():
        pmid = row.get('PMID', 'N/A')
        title = row.get('Title', 'No Title')
        journal = row.get('Journal', 'Unknown')
        year = row.get('Year', 'Unknown')
        abstract = str(row.get('Abstract', 'No Abstract Available'))
        
        # Clean abstract spaces and truncate at 1200 chars to save context window
        abstract = " ".join(abstract.split())
        if len(abstract) > 1200:
            abstract = abstract[:1200] + " ... [Truncated]"
            
        print(f"PMID: {pmid}")
        print(f"Title: {title}")
        print(f"Source: {journal} ({year})")
        print(f"Abstract: {abstract}")
        print("-" * 80)
else:
    print("No search results found. Please try again with different query. TIP: Try simpler keyword phrases.")

=== PMID: 25430706 ===

Title: Exome sequencing identifies novel ApoB loss-of-function mutations causing hypobetalipoproteinemia in type 1 diabetes.

Journal/Date: Acta diabetologica (2015)

MeSH Keywords: Adolescent, Adult, Apolipoproteins B, Base Sequence, Codon, Nonsense, Diabetes Mellitus, Type 1, Exome, Female


--- ABSTRACT ---
[AIM]: Diabetic patients commonly suffer from disturbances in production and clearance of plasma lipoproteins, known as diabetic dyslipidemia, resulting in an increased risk of coronary heart disease. The study aimed to examine the cause of hypobetalipoproteinemia in two patients with type 1 diabetes.
[METHODS]: The Diabetes Control and Complications Trial (DCCT) is a study demonstrating that intensive blood glucose control delays the onset and progression of type 1 diabetes complications. Hypobetalipoproteinemia was present in two DCCT subjects, IDs 1427 and 1078, whose LDL-C levels were 36 and 28 mg/dL, respectively, and triglyceride levels were 20 and 28 mg/dL, respectively. We performed exome sequencing on genomic DNA from the two patients with hypobetalipoproteinemia.
[RESULTS]: The subjects 1427 and 1078 had heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in the gene apolipoprotein B (ApoB), and these mutations resulted in premature stop codons at amino acid 1333 (ApoB-29) and 3680 (ApoB-81), respectively. Indeed, the plasma ApoB level of subject 1427 (19 mg/dL) was the lowest and that of subject 1078 (26 mg/dL) was the second to the lowest among all the 1,441 DCCT participants. Sequencing genomic DNA of family members showed that probands 1427 and 1078 inherited the mutations from the father and the mother, respectively.
[CONCLUSIONS]: The identification of ApoB loss-of-function mutations in type 1 diabetic patients presents innovative cases to study the interaction between hypobetalipoproteinemia and insulin deficiency.


[FULL TEXT STATUS]: Open-access full text is NOT available on PMC/PubTator for this PMID. Analysis must rely solely on the Abstract above, or search for alternative PMIDs with full-text availability.
